P2P TUI video game about space pirates playing basketball across the galaxy; built with Ratatui in Rust.

Overview — Tower defense is a video game genre where the player places and upgrades static defenses (towers, traps, units in fixed slots) to stop waves of enemies moving along paths or lanes before they reach a base, exit, or objective. The core loop is earn resources from kills or waves → build and upgrade structures with different ranges, damage types, and special effects → survive escalating waves or scripted assaults.

Context — Maps emphasize chokepoints, path length, and coverage; play is usually real-time with optional pause for planning. The genre tag fits when lane or path defense with placed structures is the main loop, not when base building and army control dominate as in a full RTS. Hybrids include MOBA lane defense, reverse tower defense (control the waves), and puzzle-action blends such as Plants vs. Zombies. Lineage runs from Dune II–style defense segments and StarCraft custom maps through standalones such as Bloons TD, Kingdom Rush, and Defense Grid.

's implementation of AI/Agent/Hook: scripts run at points in the agentic loop, synchronously — the CLI waits for every matching hook before continuing. Communication is JSON over stdin and stdout, and a stray print before the JSON breaks parsing.
Events: BeforeTool, AfterTool, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, BeforeToolSelection, AfterModel, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Notification, PreCompress.

That naming is the clearest evidence that hook events are not standardized. Gemini's BeforeTool is Claude/Code/Hook's PreToolUse and CursorAI/Hook's preToolUse, and PreCompress is what the others call compaction — three hosts, three vocabularies for the same moment.
Configured in settings.json under a hooks object, one array of definitions per event. A GeminiCLI/Extension ships them as hooks/hooks.json. Conceptual overview: Gemini CLI hooks.
's implementation of AI/Agent/Subagent: specialized agents inside the main session, each with its own system prompt, a restricted or specialized tool set, and an independent context window.
Shipped in a GeminiCLI/Extension as .md agent definition files in an agents/ directory, per the extensions reference.

Preview as of mid-2026 — the extensions reference states that sub-agents are "a preview feature currently under active development," which is the one gap keeping a Gemini extension short of a complete multi-component bundle.
GitHub/CLI/Extension that compiles Markdown workflow files into standard GitHub/Action workflows that run an AI coding agent.

Each workflow file has YAML frontmatter for triggers, permissions, tools, and the AI engine; the Markdown body tells the agent what to do. gh aw compile turns it into a .lock.yml file that Actions runs.
Engines: GitHub Copilot, Claude/Code, Codex, Google Gemini, and Pi.
Agent jobs run read-only and sandboxed by default. Writes back to GitHub go through separate safe-outputs jobs with scoped permissions.
Suited to tasks that need judgment, such as issue triage, pull request review, CI failure investigation, and keeping docs current. Builds, tests, and deploys stay in ordinary Actions workflows.
Install with gh extension install github/gh-aw.
Reading guide: gh-aw/Blog/26/01/Welcome to Peli's Agent Factory introduces GitHub Next's 100+ workflows and its 19-part Meet the Workflows tour.
By Don Syme, Peli de Halleux and Mara Kiefer, on the gh-aw blog.
GitHub Next and Microsoft Research built and run more than 100 automated agentic workflows in github/gh-aw, mostly for the gh-aw project itself and some at scale in GitHub's internal repositories.
The post calls the factory "a living library of patterns that others can study, adapt, and remix" and notes that "most repositories won't need dozens of agentic workflows."
Its 19-part tour, Meet the Workflows, describes workflows by category. Read the posts in any order and pick a workflow that matches a problem you already have.

Go Deep with Project Coordination Workflows covers finding, planning and tracking work. Plan Command breaks an issue into sub-tasks on a /plan comment, and Discussion Task Miner pulls tasks out of discussion threads.

Meet the Metrics & Analytics Workflows covers agents that watch other agents: Metrics Collector, Portfolio Analyst for cost, and Audit Workflows for other workflows' runs. These answer which workflows are worth what they cost.

Meet the Organization & Cross-Repo Workflows covers workflows that read across an organization, such as Org Health Report and Stale Repo Identifier. They need organization-level tokens, careful permissions and rate limiting.
The gh-aw Quick Start shows how to write and compile a workflow.
githubnext/agentics publishes workflows ready for gh aw add-wizard <url>, including plan.md and discussion-task-miner.md.
Several tour posts link workflow files at gh-aw v0.45.5. Compare a file with the current github/gh-aw before copying it.

Short answer: Toggle Bookmark (key b) is a Notifications-view-only feature — it is not on the PR page. It flags/unflags a notification so it persists across "mark all as read" and unread filters, letting you keep a notification visible until you deliberately deal with it.
